name: enterprise-software-ai-skills
description: A vendor-neutral library of enterprise engineering skills for AI coding agents, with the mechanical gates that keep each skill's guarantees honest.

scripts._comment_test: Explicit file list on purpose: bare `node --test` auto-discovery also matches *-test.mjs and would run check-has-test.mjs (a CLI script) as a failing 'test'; a positional glob needs Node 21+ and breaks the Node 20 leg. Explicit paths run on every Node/shell and can never silently run zero tests. Add each new test file here.

scripts._comment_check_architecture: The repo's own architecture gate, run against this repo (ADR-0015). Reads arch-gate.config.json + arch-gate.waivers.json at the root. Full scan (not --changed) because the repo is small and a full scan can never miss a pre-existing violation. Exit 0 = clean, 1 = violation, 2 = bad config/waiver. Wired as a blocking CI step in .github/workflows/test.yml and guarded by test/arch-gate-wired.test.mjs.
scripts._comment_vendor_owasp: Fetch the exact upstream OWASP cheat-sheet + GenAI text (CC-BY-SA-4.0) from source into .claude/skills/owasp-secure-coding-bdd/vendor/ (gitignored). A developer runs it to have the verbatim text offline; CI runs it (owasp-verbatim job) so the verbatim gate has source to compare against. See .claude/skills/owasp-secure-coding-bdd/vendor/NOTICE.md.
scripts._comment_check_verbatim: License-hygiene gate (ADR-0018): fail if any own-words per-sheet file contains a >=10-word run copied verbatim from its vendored CC-BY-SA source. Needs the vendored source present, so CI runs `npm run vendor:owasp` first (owasp-verbatim job in test.yml); it fails closed (exit 2) if the source is absent. Engine proven by test/owasp-verbatim.test.mjs in `npm test`.
scripts._comment_check_routing: Change-type -> required-artifact routing gate (ADR-0031): a change that touches a given kind of surface must ship the artifact that proves the matching discipline ran (a new skill needs an ADR, a new gate needs a test). Needs the change's file lists, so CI computes them from the PR diff and passes --changed-list/--added-list (.github/workflows/routing.yml). Engine proven by test/change-routing.test.mjs in `npm test`. Run locally: npm run check:routing -- --changed-list a,b --added-list a.
scripts._comment_check_links: Dangling-reference gate (ADR-0037): fail if any Markdown doc names a `.md` reference file that does not exist in the tree, so deleting or renaming a reference file can never silently orphan the links to it. Scans the whole repo by default; built-in ignores plus reference-links.config.json exclude adopter-created filenames and template placeholders, and an inline `link-check:ignore` excludes a one-off example. Engine proven by test/reference-links.test.mjs in `npm test`, which also asserts the real repo is clean.
scripts._comment_check_receipt: Skill-application receipt gate (ADR-0038): a change must carry a grounded, complete receipt in docs/skill-receipts/log.jsonl proving how each skill was applied (every skill covered; each `applied` entry cites a real skill heading and quotes >=8 exact words verbatim; coupled surfaces marked applied). Grounding, not truth: the gate prints that a human must still review. Diff binding + coupling need the PR's changed-file list (CI passes --changed-list, like routing); append-only needs --base. Engine proven by test/skill-receipt.test.mjs in `npm test`, which also validates the repo's own latest receipt against the real skills. Run locally: npm run check:receipt.
scripts._comment_prepare: Self-dogfood (ADR-0053): arm this repo's own .githooks/pre-push on `npm install`, with zero per-clone steps, by pointing core.hooksPath at .githooks. install-hooks.mjs never clobbers an existing core.hooksPath and never fails the install (ADR-0050). The hook runs the repo's fast offline gates locally before a push; CI stays the authority.
